He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Holmes grew up in [[Goodyear, Arizona]] and initially attended [[Millennium High School (Arizona)|Millennium High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-flyers-fab-freshman-daron-holmes-ii-its-all-about-where-you-fit/4UFXKVIQD5DVNJGHZXBTT7QMHA/|title=Archdeacon: Flyers' fab freshman DaRon Holmes II|first=Tom|last=Archdeacon|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=December 12, 2021|access-date=October 21, 2022}} He was named the Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 23.7 points, 10.6 rebounds, 3.8 blocks, and 3.1 assists per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/ua-target-daron-holmes-named-arizona-gatorade-player-of-the-year/article_44ddb7f4-6fd0-11ea-94c2-bbd51c6c84b7.html|title= UA target DaRon Holmes named Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year|first=Justin|last=Spears|work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=March 28, 2020|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]] prior to the start of his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/10/24/two-time-all-arizona-basketball-player-daron-holmes-commits-dayton/6023155002/|title=Two-time All-Arizona basketball player DaRon Holmes commits to Dayton|first=Richard|last=Obert|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=October 24, 2020|access-date=October 21, 2022}} He ultimately moved back to Arizona during his winter break and transferred a second time to AZ Compass Prep School in [[Chandler, Arizona]].{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/01/05/daron-holmes-transfers-montverde-academy-az-compass-prep/6557551002/|title=DaRon Holmes transfers from Montverde Academy to AZ Compass Prep|first=Richard|last=Obert|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=January 5, 2021|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] over offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], and [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]].{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-flyers-land-top-40-recruit-in-class-of-2021/F5B6GA2RKZGOZOMICAB6VMDDG4/|title=Dayton Flyers land top-40 recruit in class of 2021|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=October 24, 2020|access-date=October 21, 2022}} ==College career== Holmes started all 35 of the Dayton Flyers' games as a freshman and led the team with 12.8 points per game and also averaged 6.1 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/holmes-on-second-season-at-dayton-i-just-want-to-win/3WFWD6BY5ZB5VONFDWSOY6UTFQ/|title=Dayton Flyers forward DaRon Holmes adds weight to take his game to the next level|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=July 15, 2022|access-date=October 21, 2022}} He also set a school record with 81 total blocks in a season.{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/01/31/daron-holmes-breaks-dayton-blocked-shots-record/9288931002/|title=DaRon Holmes breaks Dayton blocked shots record|first=Richard|last=Obert|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=January 31, 2022|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes was named the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] Rookie of the Year, second-team All-Atlantic 10, and to the conference All-Defense team.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3653195/2022/10/21/dayton-basketball-anthony-grant-daron-holmes/|title=How Dayton, led by Anthony Grant and DaRon Holmes, are building on success|first=Brian|last=Hamilton|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 21, 2022|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Holmes entered his sophomore season on the watch list for the [[Karl Malone Award]].{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/daytons-holmes-named-to-watch-list-for-national-award/VHI4T5AISJHSFAE23ASJC7IFXQ/|title=Dayton’s Holmes named to watch list for national award|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=October 27, 2022|access-date=October 28, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 18.4 points, 8.1 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game and was named first-team All-Atlantic 10 team. On April 24, 2023, Holmes declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2023/04/nba-draft-daron-holmes-early-entry-testing-waters-dayton|title=Dayton center DaRon Holmes quietly declared for NBA draft while maintaining NCAA eligibility|first=Bryan|last=Kalbrosky|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 24, 2023|access-date=November 27, 2023}} He later withdrew from the draft on the day of the deadline and announced that he would return to Dayton for his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/holmes-will-return-to-dayton-after-withdrawing-from-draft/C4BP7NPMPVGAFO7QLOEPKKMRO4/|title=Holmes will return to Dayton after withdrawing from NBA Draft|first=David|last=Jablonski|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=May 31, 2023|access-date=November 27, 2023}} On May 30, 2024, Holmes declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]].[https://daytonflyers.com/news/2024/5/30/mens-basketball-mbb-all-american-daron-homes-ii-declares-for-the-nba-draft.aspx MBB All-American DaRon Holmes II Declares For The NBA Draft] On June 26, he was selected as the 22nd overall pick by the [[Phoenix Suns]], who subsequently traded him to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Ryan Dunn (basketball)|Ryan Dunn]] (No. 28), the draft rights to the 56th pick (which they later traded to the [[New York Knicks]]), a 2026 second-round selection and a 2031 second-round selection. As the No. 22 overall pick, he became the fifth Flyer to be an NBA first round draft pick.[https://daytonflyers.com/news/2024/6/26/mens-basketball-daron-holmes-ii-selected-by-the-phoenix-suns-in-the-nba-draft-traded-to-denver-nuggets.aspx DaRon Holmes II Selected By The Phoenix Suns In The NBA Draft, Traded To Denver Nuggets] ==Professional career== Holmes was selected with the 22nd overall pick by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]], however, immediately on draft night, he was traded for the 28th and 56th overall picks in the 2024 draft alongside second-round picks in 2026 and 2031{{cite web|title=Nuggets get DaRon Holmes II from Suns for Ryan Dunn, future picks|url=https://www.nba.com/news/suns-nuggets-trade-daron-holmes-ryan-dunn-2024-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 27, 2024}} and on July 9, he signed with the Nuggets.{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN DARON HOLMES II|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-daron-holmes-ii|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2024|access-date=July 18, 2024}} Three days later, he suffered a torn right [[Achilles tendon rupture|Achilles tendon]] in his Summer League debut, ending his season.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Nuggets Rookie DaRon Holmes Tears Right Achilles|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/nuggets-rookie-daron-holmes-tears-right-achilles.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 13, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}} On October 25, 2025, Holmes made his professional debut. recording 3 points and a foul in three minutes of play.{{Cite web |title=DaRon Holmes II {{!}} Forward {{!}} Denver Nuggets {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1641747/daron-holmes-ii |access-date=2026-01-24 |website=NBA |language=en}} On December 31, 2025 he scored a career-high 11 points along with 3 rebounds, 1 assist, and a block.{{Cite web |title=Denver Nuggets vs Toronto Raptors Dec 31, 2025 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/den-vs-tor-0022500468 |access-date=2026-01-24 |website=NBA |language=en}} ==Career
